ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Place two identical wooden blocks A and B, each with a mass of $4\mathrm{kg}$, on a horizontal table. The coefficient of kinetic friction for all contact surfaces is the same, $\upmu{=}0.2$. The maximum static friction is equal to the sliding friction (take $g = 10\mathrm{N/kg}$).

1. Under the horizontal pulling force $\mathrm{F}_{1}$ of 14N, what is the magnitude of the friction force $\mathrm{f}_{2}$ exerted by the ground on B? What is the magnitude of the friction force $\mathrm{f}_{1}$ exerted by B on A?
2. If A and B are placed close together on a horizontal table and a horizontal force $\mathrm{F_2}$ is applied to A to make them move together at a constant velocity, how large is $\mathrm{F_2}$? At this time, what is the elastic force exerted by A on B?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram has two configurations. In Figure 1, block A is stacked directly on top of block B, and block B rests on a horizontal rough table; a horizontal force F1 is applied to the lower block B toward the right. In Figure 2, blocks A and B are placed side by side on the horizontal rough table, with A on the left and B on the right; a horizontal force F2 is applied to A toward the right so the two blocks move together. Reasoning for Figure 1: Each block has mass m=4 kg, so the total normal force from the ground on B is (mA+mB)g=8×10=80 N. The maximum static friction from the ground on B is μN=0.2×80=16 N. Since F1=14 N is less than 16 N, the stacked blocks can remain at rest. Therefore the ground friction on B adjusts to balance the applied force, so f2=14 N. For the upper block A, there is no other horizontal force and no horizontal acceleration, so the friction exerted by B on A must be f1=0. Reasoning for Figure 2: Now A and B are side by side and move together at constant velocity, so the net force on each block is zero. Each block rests on the ground separately, so each experiences kinetic friction μmg=0.2×4×10=8 N opposite the motion. For the two-block system, F2 must balance the two ground-friction forces: F2=8+8=16 N. For block B alone, the rightward contact/elastic force exerted by A must balance B's 8 N ground friction, so the elastic force exerted by A on B is 8 N.
